'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**The [[International Criminal Court]] announces that it will pave the way for investigations into alleged [[war crime]]s in [[Palestinian territories]]. [[Israel]] and groups like [[Hamas]] could be investigated. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/international-criminal-court-paves-way-israel-war-crimes-investigation-n1256900 (NBC News)]
*[[Mali War]], [[Takuba Task Force]]
**[[Swedish Army|Swedish troops]] are deployed to [[Mali]] to join French-led [[counter-insurgency]] operations against jihadist groups. The [[Riksdag]] approved the deployment  of up to 150 soldiers in June 2020. [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20210205-swedish-troops-join-french-led-takuba-task-force-in-mali (France 24)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[American Rescue Plan]]
***The [[United States Senate]] votes 51–50 to pass a [[budget resolution]] as a step to pass the [[United States dollar|$]]1.9 trillion [[American Rescue Plan|stimulus package]] without [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] support, with [[Kamala Harris]] casting her first [[List of tie-breaking votes cast by the vice president of the United States|tiebreaking vote]] as [[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/covid-relief-package-senate-passes-budget-plan/ (CBS News)]
***The [[United States House of Representatives]] votes 219–209 to approve the Senate's budget resolution, with all Republicans and one [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] voting against the resolution. [https://thehill.com/homenews/house/537534-house-passes-budget-resolution-paving-way-for-bidens-covid-relief-plan (''The Hill'')]
**[[Economy of Indonesia]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
***[[Indonesia]]'s [[Gross Domestic Product|GDP]] contracts 2.07% in 2020, the first economic contraction since the aftermath of the [[1997 Asian financial crisis]] in 1998. [https://economy.okezone.com/amp/2021/02/05/320/2356905/ekonomi-indonesia-2020-minus-2-07-terparah-sejak-krisis-1998?_gl=1*c12qqh*_ga*UjFad1ZwZU9hY283WHNEWnRtYXM3ZTZnRjdRa21keF96QXZjSlQwM3VScmIxNG5yV1Vpd3RkeVRMdDFOX1pkSQ.. (Okezone)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Community of Madrid]], [[Lineage P.1]]
*****[[Spain]] reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant in a 44-year-old man who travelled from [[Brazil]] to [[Madrid]] on January 29 and later tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20210205/detectado-primer-caso-variante-brasilena-madrid/2073401.shtml (RTVE)]
****[[Spain]] approves the use of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] in people aged 18 to 55. [https://www.elmundo.es/ciencia-y-salud/salud/2021/02/05/601d8ef721efa0212a8b45a2.html (''El Mundo'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] imposes a ten-day curfew in [[Attica (region)|Attica]], [[Thessaloniki (regional unit)|Thessaloniki]], and [[Halkidiki]], and also closes high schools in these areas beginning tomorrow in an attempt to reduce the number of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/262066/article/ekathimerini/news/greece-imposes-earlier-curfew-closes-stores-on-weekends-to-stem-infection-rate (Ekathimerini)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Prime Minister of Poland|Prime Minister]] [[Mateusz Morawiecki]] announces that hotels, theatres, swimming pools and other indoor facilities will be allowed to reopen at 50 percent capacity on February 12, but that restaurants and fitness centres will continue to remain closed. [https://www.thenationalherald.com/coronavirus/arthro/poland_to_partially_reopen_with_conditions_next_week-1730381/ (''The National Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] secures 12 million doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] developed by [[AstraZeneca]] and [[Novavax]]. [https://www.unian.info/politics/covid-19-vaccine-delivery-plans-for-12-mln-doses-confirmed-11311436.html (UNIAN)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
*****[[India]] reaches past 5 million vaccinations. [https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/india-fastest-country-to-reach-5-mn-covid-vaccinations-mark-health-min-121020501960_1.html (''Business Standard'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bahrain]]
****[[Bahrain]] announces that all indoor gyms, indoor exercise classes, sports halls, and swimming pools will be closed from February 7 to February 21 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. The country also announces that government entities and institutions can allow up to 70 percent of their employees to [[work from home]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1804456/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] announces that it will ease its [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] measures beginning February 7. People will no longer be restricted to within one kilometer of their homes, many services will be allowed to operate, and all national parks will reopen. However, international borders will remain closed until February 20. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-02-israel-ease-lockdown-covid.html (MedicalXpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] surpasses 80,000 cases of COVID-19. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20210205000207 (''The Korea Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[Western Australia]] lifts a five-day lockdown in [[Perth]] and surrounding areas after it reports no community cases. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/western-australia-coronavirus-mark-mcgowan-lifts-lockdown-as-raft-of-restrictions-kick-in/d83a1d0b-49c3-43c2-9d19-eabe6b48cd83 (9 News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****[[Immigration New Zealand|Immigration]] and [[government of New Zealand|government]] officials announce that [[New Zealand]] will restart its Refugee Quota Programme this month, nearly a year after closing its border due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/435867/small-groups-of-refugee-families-to-be-allowed-into-new-zealand (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iowa]]
****[[Governor of Iowa|Iowa Governor]] [[Kim Reynolds]] announces that the [[Iowa|state]] will lift its [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] and gathering restrictions, which will take effect on Sunday. [https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/2021/02/05/kim-reynolds-lifts-mask-mandate-requirement-other-restrictions-rules-sunday-iowa-restaurants/4412633001/ (''The Des Moines Register'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oklahoma]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****[[Oklahoma]] reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant originated from [[Brazil]] in a woman who had a travel history. [https://kfor.com/news/coronavirus/oklahoma-confirms-first-known-case-of-brazilian-variant/ (KFOR-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Virginia]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Virginia]] reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person from eastern Virginia. [https://richmond.com/news/local/virginia-reports-first-case-of-another-covid-variant-northam-says-now-is-not-the-time/article_daa19d83-6a2e-56c4-a306-394a34b990e8.html (''Richmond Times-Dispatch'')]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
****[[AstraZeneca]]-[[University of Oxford|Oxford]] developers say that their [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine candidate]] is effective against the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|UK variant]] of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/health-55951920 (BBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Palau]] announces its intention to withdraw from the [[Pacific Islands Forum]] after claiming [[Electoral fraud|fraudulence]] in the recent election for the organization's [[Secretary General of the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat|Secretary General]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/australianz/key-pacific-body-in-crisis-as-palau-walks-out (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Crime in London]]
**2021 Croydon stabbings
***A man is killed and 10 others are injured in stabbing attacks in [[Croydon]], [[London]], [[England]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-55959214 (BBC News)]
*Aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**Prominent [[National League for Democracy]] official [[Win Htein]] is arrested for [[sedition]] and taken from his house in [[Yangon]] by members of the [[Tatmadaw|military]] and police. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/05/aung-san-suu-kyi-aide-arrested-after-saying-myanmar-coup-was-not-wise (''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]], [[Libyan peace process]]
**Delegates of the [[United Nations]]-supported Libyan Political Dialogue Forum vote in [[Geneva]] to elect [[Mohamed al-Menfi|Mohammad Younes Menfi]] as President of the Presidency Council and businessman Mohammed Dbaiba as Prime Minister, defeating President of the [[House of Representatives (Libya)|House of Representatives]] [[Aguila Saleh]], and Interior Minister [[Fathi Bashagha]]. [https://www.bloombergquint.com/markets/libyan-rivals-agree-on-new-leadership-to-govern-until-elections (Bloomberg)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Censorship in Myanmar]]
**The [[military junta]] in [[Myanmar]] orders [[Internet in Myanmar|internet service providers]] to block [[Twitter]] and [[Instagram]] "until further notice". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics-twitter/myanmar-military-rulers-order-block-on-twitter-instagram-until-further-notice-idUSKBN2A52DI?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Scientists belonging to a [[Germany|German]]–[[Madagascar|Malagasy]] expedition announce the discovery of ''[[Brookesia nana]]'', a lizard found in Madagascar. The male's body spanning only {{convert|13.5|mm|in|1}}, is potentially the smallest [[reptile]] on Earth. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-55945948 (BBC News)]
